name: Keisha Brown

five_sec.what_is_it: HelloFresh, the meal box. I did the promo one time.
five_sec.who_for: People who can pay full price after the promo. Not me.
five_sec.trust_why: Food was good for real. But 'Open a box to reveal your offer' is them playing games again.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: The green boxes. That's the box that came to my door.

full_page.what_stopped_me: The price after the promo, plus shipping. And it won't even tell you the price till you put your zip in. No EBT.

HF.quote: Girl, I did the promo box. Good food, then the price was crazy. 'Shipping fee applies on all deliveries after the first box.' Yep.

five_sec.what_is_it: An app that tells you what's for dinner.
five_sec.who_for: Moms who are tired. So, me, but with more money.
five_sec.trust_why: 90,000 families. But the button is a CEO letter, what?
five_sec.delivers_food_why: It's a menu on a phone, 'I've picked out meals for you'.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Pricing page: $25 a month. Free one only gives you 50 messages. Nothing about SNAP or what the groceries cost.
full_page.whats_missing: EBT, cost of the groceries, Aldi or Meijer.

OL.quote: 'Since using this app my grocery bills have gone down.' Cool, so why's the plan $25 a month?

five_sec.trust_why: Regular looking site. Nothing about money on the first screen though.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Says 'Choose Your Meals' and shows a phone list.

full_page.what_stopped_me: 'Try Free for 14 Days' means it costs after, and they don't say how much unless you open the question at the bottom. Pop-up wants my email for a 'special offer'.

EM.quote: I see Aldi and Meijer on there, okay. But 'Try Free for 14 Days' means it's gonna cost after, and they won't say how much.

five_sec.what_is_it: Plans dinners, texts the family, puts the list in my Instacart.
five_sec.who_for: Families that use Instacart. That's me.
five_sec.trust_why: 'Start free, no card needed' in a big button. 'Powered by Instacart' at the top.
five_sec.next_step: See a sample week, see what it costs.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Says it right there, 'We don't deliver food.' Instacart brings it, like now.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Nothing stops me trying the free part. But nowhere on the page does it say EBT or SNAP, and that's how I pay.
full_page.whats_missing: Does the cart work with my EBT card on Instacart? And will it make my order bigger?

DD.quote: Five dinners for $64 and Aldi coming up cheapest? That's what I'm talking about. But it never says EBT. Does my SNAP card work in that cart?

five_sec.who_for: People who save a lot of recipes.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Lady writing a list. No food boxes.

full_page.what_stopped_me: $5.95 a month after the 14 days. And I gotta bring my own recipes.
full_page.whats_missing: A free plan, EBT, cost of the groceries for a week.

PTE.quote: Nice app, but 'Only $5.95/mo' ain't 'only' when SNAP's gone by week three.

dd_offer.why: 'Free forever' and 'free for 14 days' on the same screen made me stop. Had to read the FAQ to get that the 14 days is just the texting part.
dd_offer.expect_day_15: The family texting thing goes away and I keep the free planner. They don't have my card so they can't charge me.

head_to_head.reason: It's free for real and it shows what the week's groceries cost, with Aldi cheapest.

EM.reason: DinnerDrop is $0 and shows it; eMeals is a trial that hides the price.

HF.reason: A box I can't afford versus a list I can pay for with what I've got.

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Home page FAQ 'Questions parents ask': add 'Can I pay with EBT/SNAP?' with a straight answer about the Instacart and Walmart carts.
